body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'm working in a company that heavily uses MongoDB and MongoDB Atlas. So it makes sense for us to run everything through MongoDB as our primary data store specially when it comes to backup / restore, you don't want to have multiple databases.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would say, there is support for casandra and sql databases, it shows there should be some way ( maybe easy way ) to use Atlas as persistent layer.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We are already using python celery in other part of our business services, but we are looking for alternatives and this can help us to move forward with evaluations.

**Additional context**
Also, we are happy to invest into the project by providing development capacity for this task. Let me know if that could be an option to consider.

comments.body: +1 for mongodb. Is this open for contribution?
Hi there, I have completed the mongodb persistence implementation. You can check the implementation details from #8908

Summary for anyone finding this issue in 2026+:

**Status: resolved via community fork, not upstream merge.**

A full MongoDB persistence plugin was submitted as [PR #8908](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/pull/8908) by @sagdelen (Jan 2026). Maintainer @bergundy declined it on policy grounds (same reasoning as the ScyllaDB proposal in [#8652](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/issues/8652#issuecomment-3775536865)): Temporal core does not accept new persistence backends.

Following that guidance, @sagdelen set up a maintained fork:

- **Fork:** [sagdelen/temporal](https://github.com/sagdelen/temporal) — current version `v1.30.0-148.3` with MongoDB persistence
- **Docker images:** `agdelen/temporal:<version>` on Docker Hub
- **Tests:** all upstream unit + integration tests run unchanged during build; functional layer validated via the [sagdelen/temporal-mongodb-tests](https://github.com/sagdelen/temporal-mongodb-tests) repo (329 feature-coverage tests using the Python SDK + omes load scenarios)
- **Backend:** MongoDB 7.0, replica set configuration, multi-document ACID transactions
- **Sync cadence:** ~every 2 months with upstream releases

This isn't an upstream integration — it's a parallel community distribution. Worth considering if you want MongoDB-backed Temporal today without forking the code yourself.
